newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices to test recent lows.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Indices to test recent lows.

text.p: Major U.S. stock indices are likely to retest recent lows, strategists said Wednesday.
Recent index options activity has done little to suggest otherwise even though some of the low put-call ratios seen in the S&P 100 index .OEX have little predictive value.
"Index option put-call ratios have gone down," said Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at EVEREN Securities. "On the
surface you would choose to look at that as bearish, but what it proves is that there is so much more hedging going on and it's not the speculative indicator that it was a while back," he said.
Throughout the market's recent slide, major index call volume has been consistently higher than put volume, suggesting investors were not too concerned with the decline.
Market strategists typically look for a sharp rise in investor bearishness, which could be signaled by an increase in put option volume, as one indication of a market upturn.
"Everybody in the whole world has been buying calls in here for a week," said Timothy Ord, editor of the Ord Oracle in Walton, Nebraska.
But with hedging and other types of arbitrage using major indices growing in popularity, index put-call ratios have lost some of their predictive value, analysts said.

Ord said another indicator he follows has suggested retail investors were willing to buy the market and were not shaken by the decline, which took the bellwether Dow industrial average from a record intraday of 7,112 on March 11 to 6,405 on April 4.
"That's not a good long-term sign," Ord said.
He said he went short Wednesday morning when June S&P 500 futures reached about 773 and his uptick reading reached 619.
He said a bearish candlestick chart pattern, which would be formed even if the market closed unchanged, would confirm the sell signal.
A rally past the 780 area on June S&Ps would be needed to negate the sell signal, Ord said.

By about 1300 CST/1800 GMT, June S&P 500 futures were down 1.55 at 770.50. Fair value was pegged at about 5.75 points over cash, with arb buy programs at about a 6.35-point premium and sell programs near a 4.35-point premium.
The spot S&P 500 index .SPX was nearly unchanged at 765.46. The Dow industrials .DJI were off 10 at 6,599.
Nie said the 6,600 to 6,650 is likely to be the Dow's upper boundary for the near term, with the 6,650 area being a previous support zone.
He said a retest of the recent low in the 6,400 area "would be typical action in a market that's in the process of moving from a selloff to a sideways pattern."
But Chris Cadbury of Cadbury Fax Service said in a report recent odd-lot short sales data and the CBOE equity put-call ratio are two indicators suggesting a retest will not occur.
